summary: The engine's failed-folder record is now a sealed record class, UnreadableFolder(Entry, Win32Error, Kind), with an internal constructor and get-only properties. It has a public enum UnreadableKind { NothingListed, ListedPartway }, and Scanner.FolderDone sets the kind from ChildCount > 0. A new WPF-free file, src/FsAnalyser.App/UnreadableRows.cs, is linked into Core.Tests. It builds one row per distinct Entry (the first occurrence wins), sorts them by a total path order in which the separator ranks lowest, and applies no cap. Each row has a kind label and a reason: a plain phrase for the three code families, otherwise Windows' message on one line followed by '(Windows error N)', with an explicit fallback when the message is empty. MainWindow now uses Build, and the tab header counts rows. Both declared rules are now twinned entries above the first settled marker in fitness.yaml, each with an xUnit Fact and plant rows F27–F29. The full suite (478), rules-parity, the full rules harness (59/59 rows) and window cases S-001/S-007/S-009 all pass, and the published exe on real folders shows the new rows.

files.why: New public enum UnreadableKind { NothingListed, ListedPartway }, whose doc comment records the M2 limitation. UnreadableFolder becomes a sealed record class with an internal constructor and get-only Entry/Win32Error/Kind (M3).
FolderDone's error branch sets the kind from _store.ChildCount(folder) > 0, the same rule TopLevelTracker and FolderTreeNode use.

The view's only logic: UnreadableRow(Path, Kind, Win32Error, Reason) with Text/ToString, plus Build (dedup by Entry, sorted with ComparePaths, no cap), KindText, Reason / Reason(int, Func) with the winerror.h-named phrase table, one-line messages, the decimal code and the empty-message fallback. No System.IO.

The inline Select is replaced by UnreadableRows.Build(result.Unreadable, result.Store.GetPath). The header N is now rows.Count. The nested UnreadableRow record is removed; PathOf and RevealMode still reach Path/Text on the new type.
Compile link for src/FsAnalyser.App/UnreadableRows.cs, next to the other linked App text files.

Unit tests for cases 1–5 and 10–13: one row per kind, repeats, 10,050 shuffled entries, separator-straddling and d2/d10 order, case-only paths, the per-code family theory with an existence check, other codes, no-message codes, the injected empty/multiline message, and the 1..16000 sweep.

The deny-ACL assertion now expects NothingListed with code 5. A new real-tree test feeds a partway failure through the ScanFailingPartway failpoint, asserts ListedPartway with children in the store, and checks that Build gives both labels.
ScanFailingPartway made internal so the engine kind test reuses the same failpoint.
A positional construction site the design did not list: the partway 995 folder now expects UnreadableKind.ListedPartway.
Two new Facts: TheUnreadableViewTouchesNoFileSystem (8 patterns, including the m4 additions) and TheAppNeverDecidesAFailedFolderKind (the ternary pattern).

The two twinned entries go above the first '# settled by' marker, single-quoted, with (?m) and including_comments: true. The block the engine appended under '# settled by SL-087' is replaced by a comment saying where the rules went and why.
Plant rows F27 (File.Exists in UnreadableRows.cs), F28 (Path.Exists with implicit usings) and F29 (a ternary-chosen kind in MainWindow); the _note is updated to 46 rows.

obligations.how: UnreadableRowsTests.ANothingListedAndAPartwayEntryGiveOneRowEachWithTheirOwnKind builds a record with one NothingListed and one ListedPartway entry and compares the rows one to one: path from pathOf, kind from the record, reason, and the exact Text.

UnreadableRowsTests.AnEntryRecordedThreeTimesIsOneRowWithItsFirstKindAndCode: Entry 4 appears three times with different codes and kinds. It gives one row with the first occurrence's NothingListed/5, and the path lookup is asked once per folder.

UnreadableRowsTests.TenThousandAndFiftyShuffledEntriesAreAllListedInPathOrder: 10,050 entries in seeded-shuffle order. Asserts exactly 10,050 rows, the same path set, every consecutive pair strictly in ComparePaths order, and every Text a real row (no overflow line).

UnreadableRowsTests.SiblingsThatStraddleTheSeparatorSortAfterTheFolderAndEverythingInIt (Theory) pins [a, a\b, a b, a.b, d1\x, d10, d2], the design's ['C:\A','C:\a\b','C:\a b','C:\a.b','C:\B'] case, and a mixed '/' and '\' case.
UnreadableRowsTests.PathsThatDifferOnlyInCaseSortTheSameWhateverTheRecordOrder feeds readme/README/ReadMe in four record orders and gets the same ordinal tie-broken order each time.
UnreadableFolderTests.AFolderThatCannotBeListedIsRecordedAndItsSiblingsAreCounted (a real temp tree with a deny ACL) now asserts new UnreadableFolder(entry, 5, UnreadableKind.NothingListed).

UnreadableFolderTests.AFolderListedPartwayIsRecordedAsListedPartwayAndTheListSaysSo: a real temp tree through TopLevelRowTextTests.ScanFailingPartway. Asserts ListedPartway/995 with 1..1999 children in the store and NothingListed/5 for the denied sibling, and that Build's rows read 'could not be opened: access denied' and 'only partly read: ... (Windows error 995)'. This also settles the design's decidable disagreement: on a finished scan the listed children are in the store when the record is written.

UnreadableRowsTests.ACodeOfAPlainFamilyGetsItsPhrase has one InlineData per code (22 rows). It checks exact phrase equality and that no number appears. It also checks each code has a Windows message (review m3). 22/22 pass.

UnreadableRowsTests.AnotherCodeGetsWindowsOwnMessageAndItsNumber over 2, 362, 363, 1920, 1921 and 4390–4394: Reason == Win32Exception(code).Message.Trim() + ' (Windows error N)', and the code is not in the phrase table.

UnreadableRowsTests.ACodeWithNoMessageStillNamesItsNumber over 9999, 15999 and 65535 gives the runtime's 'Unknown error (0x..)' text followed by ' (Windows error N)'. The 1..16000 sweep (EveryCodeUpTo16000HasAOneLineReasonAndOutsideThePhrasesNamesItsCode) covers the rest.

UnreadableRowsTests.AnEmptyOrBrokenSystemMessageStillGivesAOneLineReason feeds null, '', whitespace and CR/LF-only messages through the internal Reason(int, Func) overload and gets 'no description from Windows (Windows error 4390)'. Multi-line messages come out on one line.

Fitness entry 'TheUnreadableViewTouchesNoFileSystem (*.cs)', its xUnit twin and plant rows F27 (File.Exists beside the Win32Exception lookup) and F28 (Path.Exists) were run through eng/rules-harness/harness.py against the real taad3.fitness. The clean baseline had 0 hits in both engines, so the Win32Exception line stays quiet. F27/F28 fire in both engines (AS-RECORDED), and rules-parity says AGREE.

M1: the sweep over 1..16000 checks that every code is non-empty and has no line break, and that only codes outside the phrase table end with '(Windows error N)'. Phrases carry no number, and the #4 theory checks exact equality.

M2 fallback as decided: the public enum is { NothingListed, ListedPartway }, and its doc comment records the known limit that a folder that opened and failed before its first entry is NothingListed ('could not be opened'). The opened bit from DirectoryReader and the CfProvider measurement are deferred to a later slice per the decision (see follow_ups). The real Temp scan shows 28 code-363 rows labelled 'could not be opened'; their failing phase is still unmeasured.

M3: UnreadableFolder is a sealed record class with an internal constructor and get-only properties, so the App cannot construct a record or change its kind with 'with'. Rule 2 drops the new-UnreadableFolder pattern and keeps the ternary pattern with (?m), including_comments: true, placed above the first marker. It has an xUnit twin and plant F29, which fires in both engines.

Recorded here, since the design record is not in the repo. Get-Culture en-IN; Get-UICulture en-US; GetUserDefaultUILanguage 0x0409, GetSystemDefaultUILanguage 0x0409, GetThreadLocale 0x4009, GetUserDefaultLCID 0x4009. FormatMessage with 0x4009 fails with 15100/15105 (no en-IN message table), and the langId-0 text equals the 0x0409 text for 2, 5, 363 and 1920. So the precondition holds only where every language in the langId-0 search yields English, as here: locale en-IN has no table and falls through to en-US, which is also the display language. The #5 language clause is not verified beyond this, and the #5 theory does not cover it; the test's doc comment says so.

m3: the table is declared with winerror.h names (ERROR_BAD_NETPATH = 53 and so on), and the #4 theory also asserts that Win32Exception(code).Message does not start with 'Unknown error'. All 22 codes pass.

m4: \bPath\.Exists\b, \bnew\s+(StreamReader|StreamWriter)\b and \b(DriveInfo|RandomAccess|File(System)?Info)\. were added identically to the yaml and the twin. Recorded: Directory.Build.props:5 sets ImplicitUsings=enable, so System.IO is in scope with no token. Plant F28 (Path.Exists) proves the new pattern fires.

m5: Reason turns each CR/LF run, with the whitespace around it, into one space and trims. The sweep asserts no '\r' or '\n' for 1..16000. '%n' inserts are left alone: measured 414 codes in 1..16000 whose message contains %n, none of them among the folder-open codes (2, 3, 5, 32, 33, the network family, 362, 363, 1920, 1921, 4390–4394).
m7: the literal per-character order is kept, and the ComparePaths doc comment says it is not Explorer's numeric order ('d10' before 'd2'). A d2/d10 pair is in the pinned order Theory.

cases.test_name: eng/rules-harness plants.json F27 and F28: TheUnreadableViewTouchesNoFileSystem (*.cs) planted with File.Exists and Path.Exists in UnreadableRows.cs, Win32Exception left in place

deviations: M2 and M3, as the person decided: UnreadableFolder is a sealed record class with an internal constructor and get-only properties, not a positional record struct. The enum is { NothingListed, ListedPartway }, not { NotOpened, ListedPartway }.

Rule placement and names: the engine had appended the two declared rules as SETTLED entries at the end of fitness.yaml, with no (?m) and no including_comments. The design and spike require twinned entries above the first '# settled by' marker. They were moved there and named after their Facts, 'TheUnreadableViewTouchesNoFileSystem (*.cs)' and 'TheAppNeverDecidesAFailedFolderKind (*.cs)', because harness.py's base() pairs a yaml entry with its xUnit Fact by name and the yaml header requires that convention. The engine-appended settled block is replaced by a comment under '# settled by SL-087' saying where they went.

Interop pattern spelled '\[\s*(Dll|Library)Import\b' rather than the declared '\[\s*(DllImport|LibraryImport)\b'. It matches the same text. With the literal words spelled out, the pattern would put 'DllImport' inside ArchitectureRulesTests.cs and break the existing rule 'InteropLivesOnlyInNative (tests)', whose pattern is (Library|Dll)Import.
Rule 2 no longer carries '\bnew\s+UnreadableFolder\s*\(' (dropped per M3; the compiler holds it), and its ternary pattern names NothingListed instead of NotOpened.
The design listed two positional construction sites (Scanner.cs:284, UnreadableFolderTests.cs:27). There was a third, CancelledFolderTests.cs:211, now updated to expect ListedPartway.
TopLevelRowTextTests.ScanFailingPartway was changed from private to internal so the engine kind test reuses the same failpoint rather than copying it.
The test link is 'Linked\UnreadableRows.cs', not the design's 'App\UnreadableRows.cs', to match the existing links in the csproj.
The internal Reason overload takes Func<int, string?>, not Func<int, string>, so the test can inject null as well as empty or whitespace text.
not_built: M2's full fix is deferred by the person's decision: carrying an 'opened' bit out of DirectoryReader's ReadOutcome, and measuring the 28 code-363 rows with the CfProvider rig. Only the fallback was built: the rename to NothingListed and the documented limitation.
m1 is deferred by decision: no ChildCount ban over App, and FolderTreeNode/TopLevelTracker still compute the kind themselves instead of reading the stamped Kind.
The folder tree's wording ('could not be read in full') is not aligned with the list's 'only partly read'. The design leaves that to a later slice.

Cases C-008 (opened, then failed before the first entry) and C-009 (scan stopped mid-listing) were not material and have no dedicated test. C-008 is the documented NothingListed limitation. For C-009, Build takes no scan status, so a stopped scan's record goes through the same code.
follow_ups: Carry an 'opened' bit out of DirectoryReader to FolderDone so a folder that opened and failed before its first entry stops reading 'could not be opened'. Move the tree, the top-level rows and this list together. On this PC, 28 real code-363 rows under %TEMP%\fsa-guard-tests currently read 'could not be opened: The cloud file metadata is corrupt and unreadable. (Windows error 363)', and their failing phase is unmeasured.
Switch FolderTreeNode.Note and TopLevelTracker to read UnreadableFolder.Kind (review m1), and align the tree's 'could not be read in full' with the list's 'only partly read'.

The largest-files and kinds captions still count result.Unreadable.Count (raw record entries), while the tab header now counts distinct rows. They differ only if the engine ever records an entry twice, which FolderDone does not today.

Done-when #5's 'user's display language' is verified only on a machine whose languages all resolve to English messages (display en-US; regional format en-IN with no message table, so FormatMessage falls through to en-US). A machine whose display language differs from its regional format and install language is needed to check it.
414 Windows messages in 1..16000 contain unfilled %n inserts. None is a code a folder open is known to return. If a scan ever records one, the row shows the '%1' literally.

Scratch hygiene: a real scan of %TEMP% found 43 failed folders left behind by earlier test runs (fsa-guard-tests cloud placeholders with 363/1920, fsa-window-cases denied folders). Those scripts' cleanup (C-005 scratch-folder hygiene) is worth a look.
Rule 2 catches only a ternary-chosen kind. A switch expression or an if/else that picks an UnreadableKind in App code passes it (named in the Fact's comment).

59 rows, 59 AS-RECORDED, 0 stray hits, exit 0 (plants F01–F29, P, S and divergence rows D1–D13).
